biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan is an Emirati royal and military-trained statesman whose standing derives from Abu Dhabi's ruling Al Nahyan dynasty. A son of UAE founder Sheikh Zayed, he trained at Sandhurst, served across the armed forces and became crown prince in 2004. He succeeded his brother as Ruler of Abu Dhabi and was elected President of the UAE in May 2022, placing him at the centre of the federation's political and economic leadership.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Roman Arkadyevich Abramovich is a Russian-born businessman and investor whose fortune took shape during the post-Soviet privatization of state assets. In 1995, he and partners acquired control of oil producer Sibneft; a decade later he sold a 73% stake to Gazprom. He later diversified through holdings in steel and nickel, served as governor of Chukotka, and became internationally known through his 19-year ownership of Chelsea F.C.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Roman Arkadyevich Abramovich is a Russian-Israeli businessman and politician worth billions of dollars. Abramovich is the founder and majority shareholder of Millhouse LLC, a private investment firm, and is best known outside of Russia as the owner of Chelsea F.C., a Premier League football team. From 2000 to 2008, he was the Governor of Chukotka Autonomous Okrug.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum is an Emirati royal and statesman born into Dubai’s Al Maktoum ruling family. Prepared for government from youth, he became head of Dubai Police in 1968 and the UAE’s first defence minister in 1971. He later helped steer Dubai’s growth through its airport, Jebel Ali Free Zone and the launch of Emirates airline, before succeeding his brother as ruler in 2006 and becoming UAE vice president and prime minister.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan is an Emirati royal, investor and public official from Abu Dhabi's ruling family, whose dynastic wealth grew from the emirate's oil resources. His personal holdings include Newton Investment and Development, the majority owner of City Football Group, while his chairmanships of Mubadala and the Emirates Investment Authority are sovereign roles rather than personal assets. He also serves as UAE Vice President, with Manchester City making him internationally recognisable.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed bin Sultan bin Zayed bin Khalifa Al Nahyan is an Emirati politician and member of the Abu Dhabi royal family. He is the deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates, minister of presidential affairs, and a millionaire. He is the half-brother of UAE President Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, and he is married to one of the daughters of Dubai ruler Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Alisher Usmanov is an Uzbekistan-born Russian industrial investor who made his first fortune producing scarce plastic bags in the late Soviet period. He later built his core wealth through a series of acquisitions in iron ore and steel, assembled as Metalloinvest, before grouping mining, telecommunications and technology interests under USM. Early investments in Facebook and other technology companies broadened the portfolio, while fencing administration and cultural philanthropy became prominent later chapters.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Gulbakhor Burkhanovna Ismailova is an Uzbek-born retired gynaecologist who spent her medical career in Tashkent. Her public financial profile is not linked to a documented business career, but to family trusts associated with her brother, industrialist Alisher Usmanov. Authorities identified her as a settlor and, historically, a beneficiary in structures connected to major assets including Dilbar; her representatives say she later irrevocably renounced any future benefit from those trusts.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said is Oman's head of state and a member of the Al Bu Said dynasty. After completing Oxford's Foreign Service Programme, he worked in the foreign ministry, served as its secretary-general, and spent eighteen years as minister of heritage and culture. Sultan Qaboos named him as successor, and Haitham took the throne in January 2020. His position derives from dynastic succession and decades of public service, not a documented entrepreneurial fortune.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Oman's Sultan is Haitham bin Tariq Al Said. Prior to becoming Sultan, he spent decades in the Cabinet of his cousin, Sultan Qaboos bin Said. From 2002 until 2020, he served as The minister of Heritage and Culture. In his will, Sultan Qaboos appointed Haitham as his successor, and he was crowned sultan on January 11, 2020, few hours after Qaboos passed.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan is an Emirati royal, investor and national-security official whose financial base lies in Abu Dhabi's oil-derived ruling-family wealth. He expanded that position through Royal Group, a family office that controls a majority of listed conglomerate IHC, while separately chairing the government-owned sovereign investors ADIA and ADQ. He also serves as Abu Dhabi's Deputy Ruler and UAE National Security Adviser, and chairs the artificial-intelligence group G42.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Prince Abdulaziz bin Fahd Al Saud is the youngest son of Saudi Arabia’s late King Fahd and a former minister of state. He also served as chief of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers’ Court, placing him close to the machinery of government. His private wealth is opaque: court-based reporting links companies associated with him to a substantial United States property portfolio, but public evidence does not justify treating Saudi sovereign or wider royal-family assets as his personal holdings.

biography.label: Biography
biography.value: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan is an Emirati royal and diplomat, and a son of UAE founder Sheikh Zayed. After studying political science at UAE University, he entered federal service, first as an undersecretary and then as minister of information and culture. He became foreign minister in 2006 and deputy prime minister in 2024, placing him at the centre of the federation's international diplomacy. His standing derives from the Al Nahyan dynasty and public office, not a publicly documented entrepreneurial fortune.
